commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. content.text:
The header now reads "92% aligned" (100% minus the divergence score), and I cleaned up the panel's look. I checked it with screenshots of the real app in all three states: running, Report tab and Source tab. They used made-up agent output, not a real `claude` run.

**Alignment wording**
- **Header:** the score sits after a thin divider beside "Divergence", in a lighter weight than before, with "3 hours ago" beside it in muted text. It's coloured green, amber or red as before. The separate "Aligned/Drifting/Diverged" word is gone, since the percentage now says it.
- **Elsewhere:** the Report tab's first figure is now "Aligned", and saved reports show "N% aligned". This keeps one number throughout instead of mixing "8% divergence" with "92% aligned". Per-file divergence percentages are unchanged.

**Visual cleanup**
- **Header:** it's a fixed height, so it no longer grows when the score appears after a run.
- **Tabs:** they were bordered buttons where the selected one was hard to see. They're now plain labels: muted, brightening on hover, and underlined when selected. They line up with the content below.
- **Report tab layout:** sections have a clear heading, with small muted labels for their parts. Everything from Assessment down is in two equal columns:
  - Assessment: Source | Spec
  - Well defined | Less well defined
  - Best defined files | Least defined files
  - Most diverged | Saved reports

  The best/least defined file lists now start level with each other; before, they were pushed down by however many areas each side had. "Most diverged" no longer stretches across the full width with a big gap before the percentages.
- **Rows:** file and saved-report text now lines up with the headings, and only the hover highlight extends past it. The tree rows and the running agents' tables were also nudged to line up with their headings.

Tests: 155 passed, 1 ignored, and 1 failed, which is the palette test that was already failing. I didn't add a test that checks the header text itself; the new `Report::alignment` calculation is covered. `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, and the app builds with no warnings. The temporary screenshot hook I used is removed.

The spec in `spec/scope/divergence/index.pi` now covers the "92% aligned" header, the underlined tabs and the two-column Report layout.
